findings.passage: “I believe that the most safe and secure elections are in person on Election Day with voter ID and paper ballot,” he said. “I also want to make sure that non-citizens don’t vote here in the state of Missouri, and then, no, I don’t trust the election machines.
findings.note: Quoted by Missourinet in a campaign interview. He links voter ID at in-person voting with a paper ballot and says he wants to keep non-citizens from voting.

findings.passage: “It says all citizens can vote in the state of Missouri. It does not say only citizens,” he said.
findings.note: Quoted by Missourinet. He explains why he backs a proposed constitutional amendment limiting voting to citizens; the outlet says he supports it.

findings.passage: Denny Hoskins has pushed for election reforms, including Missouri’s Voter ID law, that have made Missouri’s elections among the most secure in the nation.
findings.note: Campaign-site text written in the third person, issued by his campaign. Undated; it appears to be from the 2024 Secretary of State campaign.

findings.passage: Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins announced that his office used SAVE to "identify approximately 1,000 individuals registered to vote in Missouri that we could not confirm are United States citizens.”
findings.note: KCUR reports his June 2026 announcement; the quoted words are from his announcement. His office used the federal SAVE database to flag registered voters whose citizenship it could not confirm.
